newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Poll shows Argentines flexible on labor rules.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Argentines flexible on labor rules.

text.p: Most Argentines would be prepared to accept changes in their working hours and vacations depending on the needs of their employers, according to a private poll published Friday.

The survey by Mora y Araujo published in the La Nacion newspaper showed that 74 percent of Argentines would accept changes in their working hours. Fifty-nine percent thought that receiving part of their wages in a variable bonus was a better system than having just a fixed salary.

The findings come as Argentina's union movement is locked in stubborn battle with the government over its plans to free up labor rules, including measures to make working hours more flexible and allow firms to vary wages according to profits.
Labor opposition included a general strike on December 26.
The government hopes that a more flexible labor market would help reduce Argentina's 17.3-percent unemployment, but unions argue that they would erode hard-won rights for workers.
While prepared to be more flexible on some issues, 71 percent of respondents said they would reject lower pay. But 26 percent said they would accept a cut in wages.
The poll contained worrying data for the unions.
Most respondents, 57 percent, said they would be best off representing themselves in talks to fix wages with their employers, without intervention from unions.
Sixty-two percent said union leaders spend most of their energies looking after their own personal interests.
The poll of 1,959 residents of Buenos Aires was carried out last October, according to La Nacion, which did not cite the survey's margin of error.
After a long tussle with Congress, President Carlos Menem opted to pass the government's labor market measures by decree in December. But they were swiftly declared unconstitutional by the courts.
